identity.title: Pharmacologic HIF-2alpha inhibition preserves T cell effector function in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

content.abstract: Hypoxia-inducible factor 2alpha (HIF-2alpha) is a central oncogenic driver in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and a therapeutic target of the small-molecule inhibitor belzutifan. Genetic studies in murine models have suggested that hypoxia signaling may support T cell effector programs, raising concern that HIF-2alpha inhibition could impair antitumor immunity. However, whether pharmacologic HIF-2alpha inhibition alters human T cell biology remains unknown. Here, we investigated the cell-intrinsic effects of EPAS1 (encoding HIF-2alpha) perturbation in primary human T cells. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of HIF-2alpha demonstrated no notable transcriptional effects. Similarly, pharmacologic treatment with belzutifan produced minimal transcriptional changes and did not impair proliferation, cytokine production, polyfunctionality, or cytotoxic activity in T cells derived from healthy donor peripheral blood, peripheral blood from patients with ccRCC, or tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes under hypoxic conditions. High- dimensional immunophenotyping revealed preserved T cell differentiation and activation states following pharmacologic HIF-2alpha inhibition in vitro and in peripheral blood from patients receiving HIF-2alpha inhibitor therapy. Together, these findings demonstrate that pharmacologic HIF-2alpha inhibition preserves key effector programs, providing a mechanistic basis for the immunologic safety of HIF-2alpha-targeted therapy in ccRCC.
